DS_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional minimum analyst severity to fetch (Very-Low / Low / Medium / High / Very-High — the canonical Digital Shadows / Reliaquest SearchLight severity vocabulary). When supplied, the executor forwards every severity at-or-above the floor as the canonical SearchLight filter.severity list in the request body so the API itself does the server-side narrowing — e.g. DS_MIN_SEVERITY=Medium sends severity: ['Medium', 'High', 'Very-High']. Blank / missing / unparseable input keeps every incident (the typical operational mode). Operator-friendly aliases (critical / crit -> Very-High, elevated -> High, moderate / med -> Medium, vlow / very_low -> Very-Low) are normalised onto the canonical title-cased SearchLight vocabulary.

DS_LIMIT.description: Optional maximum page size for SearchLight pagination (default 100, ceiling 500 — the documented SearchLight per-request limit). Forwarded into the /incidents/find and /intel-incidents/find request body as limit: <int>. Pagination walks offset / limit until either the result set is exhausted, MAX_RESULTS (5000) is reached, or MAX_PAGES (100) is hit. Values below 1 / above 500 are clamped. The executor walks /incidents/find first then /intel-incidents/find and unions both record sets into a single Faraday host output.

name: digital_shadows
title: Digital Shadows / Reliaquest SearchLight
description: Digital Shadows / Reliaquest SearchLight importer. Pulls incident + intel-incident records from the SearchLight REST API (POST /incidents/find and POST /intel-incidents/find) and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Digital Shadows (acquired by Reliaquest and now also marketed as the Reliaquest GreyMatter Digital Risk Protection service) is a commercial external digital-risk-protection platform — analysts curate incidents around an operator's named brand / domain / email / executive footprint and publish intel incidents tied to wider threat-actor campaigns. The executor walks /incidents/find first then /intel-incidents/find and unions both record sets into a single Faraday host output. DS_MIN_SEVERITY (Very-Low / Low / Medium / High / Very-High) is optional and forwarded server-side as the canonical SearchLight filter.severity list so the API itself does the severity-narrowing. DS_LIMIT (default 100, ceiling 500) is the per-request page size. Pagination walks offset / limit in DS_LIMIT-record pages until either the result set is exhausted, MAX_RESULTS (5000) is reached, or MAX_PAGES (100) is hit; inter-page sleep paces requests at 0.5s. Auth: SearchLight uses an HMAC-SHA256 signing scheme. The operator creates an API key + secret pair in the SearchLight portal (Settings -> API -> Generate Key) and pastes the returned values into DS_KEY + DS_SECRET. For each request the dispatcher computes string_to_sign = '{epoch_ms}{HTTP_VERB}{path}{body}', HMAC-SHA256 signs that with the operator's secret, base64-encodes the signature, and sends 'Authorization: hmac {DS_KEY}:{signature}' + 'searchlight-timestamp: {epoch_ms}' on every request. The legacy 'X-DS-Timestamp' / 'X-DS-Signature' header pair is emitted in parallel for compatibility with older on-prem SearchLight installs. DS_HOST is mandatory — SearchLight runs in multiple regions (api.searchlight.app / api.eu.searchlight.app / on-prem mirrors) and silently defaulting would mask a tenant-mismatch. Each incident / intel-incident becomes one Faraday vulnerability under a single synthetic 0.0.0.0 host with hostname 'digital-shadows' (SearchLight records are brand-keyed / actor-keyed not host-keyed — the operator's other agents emit the host-side findings this feed is correlated against), tagged exactly ['digital-shadows'] per the playbook spec, with a [DigitalShadows] (or [DigitalShadows][Intel]) name prefix, the canonical type + title in the name, and the SearchLight record id in external_id. Severity is bucketed from SearchLight's published Very-Low / Low / Medium / High / Very-High ladder: Very-High -> critical / High -> high / Medium -> medium / Low -> low / Very-Low -> info. Closed / resolved / dismissed incidents are floored to 'info' regardless of the published ladder. Unscored records default to 'info'. Status is always 'open' (a SearchLight incident can be closed in the portal but the underlying external risk lives on; Faraday surfaces the finding as open so the operator's remediation workflow takes over). Resolution defaults to the SearchLight analyst-authored mitigation text when present, falling back to a type-appropriate recommendation: Phishing -> SearchLight Takedown service + egress-proxy block; Data Loss Detection -> credential reset + forensics; Brand Protection -> trademark counsel + domain-registrar takedown; Cyber Threat -> perimeter + EDR blocklist; Infrastructure -> rotate exposed secrets; VIP -> notify executive + expand monitoring. Refs include the SearchLight portal permalink, the record id, title, type, severity, status, every entity (with type prefix), actors + tags + references (intel mode), any CVE ids surfaced in title / summary / mitigation / structured cve field (each with its canonical NVD permalink), and raised / modified / occurred / published timestamps as explicit Ds-* (incidents) / DsIntel-* (intel) pivots so operators can pivot from a Faraday finding back to the SearchLight portal. Tags: [digital-shadows].
